findings.finding: Splitting the two variables removes the startup fail-closed check that the MCP authorship key currently gets for free, and the plan adds nothing in its place. Today `compose_startup_opcert_binding` reads the same `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` file, so an empty or invalid key stops MCP startup. After the change only the op-cert key is checked. The authorship key at `/run/secrets/rebar-bot-signing-key` can be an empty file, which fetch-secrets.sh writes as a 'supported unsigned state' when the SSM slot is blank. In that case `_apply_authorship` logs a warning and writes the event unsigned. A blank, mis-rotated or out-of-band-changed SSM value would quietly bring back MCP events that fail enforced `verify-identity`. The only check is the one-time post-deploy acceptance check, and nothing alarms afterwards.
